html:
1What You Will Learn

  • Match EC2 instance families, such as compute optimized and storage optimized, to workloads
  • Explain what Elastic Load Balancing and Auto Scaling do, and how they give elasticity
  • Tell Amazon ECS, Amazon EKS and Amazon ECR apart
  • Choose between AWS Fargate and AWS Lambda for serverless compute
  • Recognize Elastic Beanstalk, Lightsail, AWS Batch and AWS Outposts

2Servers, scaling and containers

Running case

Tidewater Needs Compute That Flexes

  • The shop runs on a few big servers sized for the holiday peak, and a crashed server takes it offline
  • Traffic spikes at the sale and then falls
  • Every photo upload needs a small thumbnail, and the developers want no servers for that job
  • The team is packaging the shop in containers and wants help running them
  • The warehouse needs local processing next to its scanners
  • Your job: choose the compute for each need

Compute Choices: How Much Do You Manage?

  • Virtual servers: Amazon EC2 gives the most control, and the most to manage
  • Containers: Amazon ECS and Amazon EKS run packaged applications; AWS Fargate removes the servers
  • Serverless: Fargate and AWS Lambda mean no servers to provision or manage
  • The more AWS manages, the less you patch (shared responsibility, Module 3)
  • Choose by control needed against work you want to avoid

Exam tip: Most control: EC2. Least to manage: Lambda, with containers and Fargate in between.

Amazon EC2: Virtual Servers in the Cloud

  • Amazon EC2 (Elastic Compute Cloud) provides on-demand, scalable computing capacity: virtual servers called instances
  • Launch as many or as few as you need, scale up for busy periods and scale down afterward
  • An Amazon Machine Image (AMI) is a preconfigured template with the operating system and software
  • The instance type sets the CPU, memory, storage and network capacity
  • Amazon EBS volumes keep data; instance store volumes hold temporary data that is deleted when the instance stops or terminates
  • A security group is a virtual firewall; a key pair is secure login information
  • You manage the guest operating system and its patches

Exam tip: Virtual servers where you control the operating system: Amazon EC2.

EC2 Instance Types: Match the Family to the Workload

Family Designed for Think
General purpose A balance of compute, memory and networking, such as web servers Everyday
Compute optimized Compute-intensive work on high performance processors: batch processing, media transcoding, scientific modeling CPU-bound
Memory optimized Fast performance on large data sets in memory Big in-memory data
Storage optimized High, sequential read and write access to very large data sets on local storage, with many low-latency random IOPS Disk-heavy
Accelerated computing Hardware accelerators for graphics, floating-point or pattern matching work Graphics, machine learning
  • A name such as c7g.xlarge shows the family, the generation and a size

Exam tip: Compute optimized for processing power; storage optimized for local disk speed.

Elastic Load Balancing: Sharing the Traffic

  • Elastic Load Balancing (ELB) automatically distributes incoming traffic across targets such as EC2 instances, containers and IP addresses, in one or more Availability Zones
  • It checks the health of its targets and sends traffic only to healthy ones
  • It scales its own capacity as traffic changes, raising availability and fault tolerance
  • An Application Load Balancer handles HTTP and HTTPS (layer 7); a Network Load Balancer handles TCP and UDP (layer 4)
  • It can take over encryption and decryption, using certificates from AWS Certificate Manager
  • Gateway Load Balancers exist, and the Classic Load Balancer is the previous generation Beyond the guide

Exam tip: Spread traffic across servers and skip the failed ones: a load balancer.

Auto Scaling: Elasticity on Demand Old name [Verify live]

  • Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling keeps the right number of instances for the load, in an Auto Scaling group
  • You set a minimum, a desired capacity and a maximum; the group never goes outside them
  • Scaling policies add instances as demand rises and remove them as it falls: that is elasticity
  • It replaces unhealthy instances and balances them across Availability Zones
  • New instances register with the load balancer automatically; there is no additional fee for Auto Scaling itself
  • AWS Auto Scaling scaling plans also cover other resources; As of 4 November 2026 the docs show how to migrate them to scaling policies

Exam tip: Add and remove servers automatically as demand changes: Auto Scaling.

Containers: Amazon ECS, Amazon EKS and Amazon ECR

Service What it is Remember
Amazon ECS (Elastic Container Service) Fully managed container orchestration to deploy, manage and scale containerized applications, using task definitions, tasks and services AWS's container service
Amazon EKS (Elastic Kubernetes Service) Fully managed Kubernetes: AWS manages the control plane, in AWS and in your own data centers Choose for Kubernetes
Amazon ECR (Elastic Container Registry) A managed registry to store, manage and share container images, with image scanning The image library
  • A container packages code and its dependencies so it runs the same way everywhere

Exam tip: Kubernetes: EKS. AWS container orchestration: ECS. Storing images: ECR.

AWS Fargate: Containers Without Servers

  • AWS Fargate runs containers without servers or clusters of EC2 instances to manage
  • It works with Amazon ECS: you package the app, set CPU and memory, and launch it
  • There is no choosing server types, deciding when to scale clusters or packing the cluster
  • Each Fargate task has its own isolation boundary: it does not share the kernel, CPU, memory or network interface with another task
  • It is serverless, pay-as-you-go compute for containers
  • New tasks always start on the latest patched platform revision

Exam tip: Containers with no servers to manage: AWS Fargate.

3Serverless, simple options and practice

AWS Lambda: Run Code Without Servers

  • AWS Lambda runs your code without provisioning or managing servers
  • You write a function and connect a trigger, such as Amazon API Gateway, Amazon S3, Amazon SQS or EventBridge
  • Lambda scales automatically and manages capacity, scaling and patching for you
  • You pay for requests and execution time, with no upfront commitment
  • A single invocation can run up to 15 minutes, with 128 MB to 10,240 MB of memory
  • Lambda suits short-lived, event-driven work

Exam tip: Run code when something happens, with no servers: AWS Lambda.

Elastic Beanstalk, Lightsail and AWS Batch

Service What it does Choose it when
AWS Elastic Beanstalk You upload application code; it provisions EC2 instances, sets up load balancing, health monitoring and scaling You want to deploy a web app without building the infrastructure
Amazon Lightsail Virtual private servers, containers, databases, storage and networking for a low, predictable monthly price A simple website or small project
AWS Batch Runs batch computing jobs at any scale, provisioning the compute each job needs Large queued jobs, with no batch software to manage
  • Elastic Beanstalk has no additional charge; you pay for the resources it creates

Exam tip: Upload code and let AWS build the environment: Elastic Beanstalk. Simple and predictable: Lightsail.

AWS Outposts: AWS Infrastructure on Your Premises

  • AWS Outposts extends AWS infrastructure, services, APIs and tools to your own premises
  • An Outpost is a pool of AWS compute and storage at your site that AWS operates, monitors and manages as part of an AWS Region
  • Run EC2 instances, EBS volumes, ECS clusters and RDS databases there, with the same APIs as in a Region
  • Use it for low latency and local data processing
  • A service link connects the Outpost to its Region
  • It is a hybrid deployment option (Module 6)

Exam tip: AWS-managed infrastructure inside your own data center: AWS Outposts.

What the Exam Asks: Compute

  • Compute or storage optimized: processing power, or fast local disk access
  • Load balancer or Auto Scaling: spread the traffic, or add and remove servers
  • ECS, EKS or ECR: AWS orchestration, Kubernetes, or the image library
  • Fargate or Lambda: containers with no servers, or functions with no servers
  • Beanstalk, Lightsail or Batch: upload code, a simple predictable server, or queued jobs
  • Outposts: AWS hardware in your data center
  • Elasticity: capacity that follows demand, up and down

Exam tip: Name the need, then the smallest service that meets it.

Design Check: Tidewater's Compute Plan

Tidewater's need Choose
Servers that grow for the sale and shrink afterward EC2 Auto Scaling group, behind a load balancer
Spread traffic and skip a failed server Elastic Load Balancing
A report that holds a huge data set in memory Memory optimized instance
A thumbnail for every photo upload, with no servers AWS Lambda, triggered by Amazon S3
The shop's containers, with no servers to manage Amazon ECS on AWS Fargate
A team that already runs Kubernetes Amazon EKS
A small blog at a low, predictable price Amazon Lightsail
Local processing at the warehouse, with AWS tools AWS Outposts
  • Cover the right column, answer each row yourself, then compare

4Exam Q&A

4.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer; some ask for two)

S1Tidewater runs a nightly job that converts product videos to new formats, and the job is limited by processing power. Which EC2 instance family fits best?

  • AMemory optimized, for large data sets held in memory
  • BStorage optimized, for high sequential access to local disks
  • CCompute optimized, for compute-intensive applications
  • DGeneral purpose, for an even balance of resources
Show the answer

Answer: C. Compute optimized instances are designed for compute-intensive work, and media transcoding is a listed example. Memory optimized instances target large in-memory data sets, storage optimized instances target local disk throughput, and general purpose instances suit balanced workloads.

S2Which TWO statements about EC2 instance families are correct? (Select TWO.)

  • ACompute optimized instances are designed for workloads that process large data sets in memory
  • BStorage optimized instances suit workloads that need high, sequential read and write access to local storage
  • CGeneral purpose instances offer no balance and suit only one kind of workload
  • DMemory optimized instances are designed for fast performance on large in-memory data sets
  • EAccelerated computing instances use only standard processors and no co-processors
Show the answer

Answer: B, D. Storage optimized instances serve workloads with high sequential access to local storage, and memory optimized instances serve large in-memory data sets. Processing large data sets in memory describes memory optimized rather than compute optimized, general purpose instances balance resources, and accelerated computing instances add hardware accelerators.

S3Tidewater's traffic spikes during the sale and falls afterward. Which service automatically adds EC2 instances when demand rises and removes them when it falls?

  • AAmazon EC2 Auto Scaling, using an Auto Scaling group
  • BElastic Load Balancing, using an Application Load Balancer
  • CAWS Outposts, using racks installed on its premises
  • DAmazon Lightsail, using a fixed monthly plan
Show the answer

Answer: A. EC2 Auto Scaling changes the number of instances between the minimum and maximum you set, which is elasticity. A load balancer spreads traffic across instances without adding or removing them, Outposts is AWS hardware at your site, and Lightsail offers fixed plans.

S4Which service distributes incoming traffic across EC2 instances in more than one Availability Zone and sends requests only to healthy targets?

  • AAmazon EC2 Auto Scaling, which adds and removes instances as demand changes
  • BAWS Fargate, which runs containers without any servers to manage
  • CAmazon ECR, which stores and shares container images for deployment
  • DElastic Load Balancing, which spreads traffic across healthy targets
Show the answer

Answer: D. Elastic Load Balancing distributes traffic across targets in one or more Availability Zones and routes only to healthy ones. Auto Scaling changes the number of instances, Fargate runs containers, and ECR stores container images.

S5Tidewater is packaging its shop in containers on Amazon ECS and does not want to provision or manage servers or clusters of EC2 instances. What should it use?

  • AAmazon ECR, to store and share the container images
  • BAWS Fargate, as the capacity that runs the containers
  • CAWS Batch, to queue large computing jobs
  • DAmazon EC2, with a cluster of instances it manages itself
Show the answer

Answer: B. Fargate runs containers without servers or clusters of EC2 instances to manage. ECR only stores the images, Batch is for queued computing jobs, and EC2 would leave the team managing the cluster.

S6Every time a customer uploads a product photo to Amazon S3, Tidewater needs a thumbnail created automatically, without running any servers. Which service fits best?

  • AAmazon EC2, with an instance that runs all day
  • BAmazon Lightsail, with a small virtual private server
  • CAWS Lambda, with a function started by the upload
  • DAWS Elastic Beanstalk, with a web application environment
Show the answer

Answer: C. Lambda runs code in response to events such as an upload, needs no servers, and charges only for requests and execution time. An always-on instance, a Lightsail server or a Beanstalk environment would all keep servers running.

S7Tidewater's developers want to upload the code of a web application and have AWS provision the instances, set up load balancing and scale the environment. Which service fits best?

  • AAWS Elastic Beanstalk, which deploys the uploaded code
  • BAWS Batch, which runs large queued computing jobs
  • CAWS Outposts, which places AWS hardware on premises
  • DAmazon ECR, which stores container images
Show the answer

Answer: A. With Elastic Beanstalk you upload the code, and it provisions the instances and configures load balancing, health monitoring and scaling. Batch runs queued jobs, Outposts is AWS infrastructure at your site, and ECR is an image registry.

5Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
EC2 virtual servers; families match workloads, such as compute optimized and storage optimized
Elasticity a load balancer shares traffic across healthy targets; Auto Scaling adds and removes instances
Containers ECS orchestrates, EKS runs Kubernetes, ECR stores images
Serverless Fargate runs containers without servers; Lambda runs functions on events
Simple options Elastic Beanstalk deploys uploaded code, Lightsail is simple and predictable, Batch runs queued jobs
Hybrid Outposts puts AWS infrastructure in your data center
